claims.text: Pre-exposure Q235 steel ordinarily contains MnS inclusions.
A refined deoxidation/cleaning heat treatment can reduce the density of MnS inclusions in Q235 steel.
MnS inclusions in untreated Q235 steel act as preferential anodic sites.
MnS inclusions form local galvanic microcells in Q235 steel.
Galvanic activity associated with MnS inclusions enhances localized dissolution.
Galvanic activity associated with MnS inclusions promotes pit nucleation.
Reducing MnS inclusion density decreases the driving force for galvanic corrosion.
Reducing MnS inclusion density promotes more uniform passive-film formation.
Reducing MnS inclusion density slows overall corrosion kinetics in chloride-rich environments.
Q235 steel with reduced MnS inclusion density will exhibit delayed pit initiation relative to untreated Q235 steel.
Q235 steel with reduced MnS inclusion density will exhibit lower corrosion rates relative to untreated Q235 steel.
Q235 steel with reduced MnS inclusion density will exhibit more uniform passive-film development relative to untreated Q235 steel.
The corrosion differences between treated and untreated specimens will be more pronounced at approximately 70°C than at approximately 25°C.
Elevated temperature accelerates the relevant electrochemical reactions.
The proposed comparison uses untreated Q235 steel exposed under the same chloride concentration and temperature conditions as the treated steel.
The mechanism is intended to apply to chloride-rich aqueous environments at approximately 25°C and 70°C.
The interpretation requires the treated and untreated specimens to differ essentially only in MnS inclusion density.
The proposed heat treatment may alter microstructural characteristics other than MnS inclusion density that could affect corrosion.
